text: {"lessons":["I repeatedly sold winners to secure small gains, then sometimes bought Stock B back; I should let the investment thesis and valuation—not the comfort of a realized gain—guide when I sell or re-enter.","I held on until selling Stock C at a loss of about 50%, showing how painful it is for me to admit a mistake. I should judge each holding by its current prospects, not its cost basis, and reassess losses just as carefully as gains.","Frequent account checks can tempt me into unnecessary trades. I should use clear portfolio-level goals and risk limits, and trade only when new information or a meaningful change in the thesis warrants it."]}
